title: Canonical affine supported-section triangle and its localization models
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $K=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ be an ideal, allowing $r=0$, and let $L\in D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $Z=V(K)=\{\mathfrak p:K\subseteq\mathfrak p\}$ and $W=X\setminus Z$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For an $A$-module $N$, let $\Gamma_K(N)=\{x:K^n x=0\text{ for some }n\geq0\}$ [def-sbc-ideal-power-torsion-functor], and let $R\Gamma_K$ be its right derived functor. For a complex representing $L$, let $\widetilde L$ denote its termwise associated complex of quasi-coherent sheaves [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. Write $R\Gamma(W,-)$ for derived Zariski module sections [pqf-def-cohomology], and $R\Gamma_Z(X,-)$ for derived sections with support in $Z$ (the right derived functor of the kernel of restriction from $X$ to $W$). Let $T_f$ be the alternating complex with $T_f^p=\prod_{i_0<\cdots<i_p}A_{f_{i_0}\cdots f_{i_p}}$ for $0\leq p<r$, zero otherwise, and differential the signed sum $\sum_{a=0}^{p+1}(-1)^a\operatorname{res}_a$. Here $A_g$ is localization at the powers of $g$. Let $E_f=[A\longrightarrow T_f^0\longrightarrow T_f^1\longrightarrow\cdots]$ with $A$ in degree zero and the diagonal augmentation. Derived tensors use a K-flat resolution [def-pc-kflat-complex]. There are canonical isomorphisms
$$R\Gamma_K(L)\cong R\Gamma_Z(X,\widetilde L)\cong E_f\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}L,\qquad R\Gamma(W,\widetilde L|_W)\cong T_f\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}L.$$
They identify the augmented localization complexes with the distinguished triangle
$$R\Gamma_K(L)\longrightarrow L\longrightarrow R\Gamma(W,\widetilde L|_W)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_K(L)[1],$$
whose middle arrow is restriction. These are the derived-functor comparisons induced by the augmentations, natural in $L$, rather than unspecified isomorphisms. For ideals $K_1,K_2$ with $V(K_1)\subseteq V(K_2)$, the natural support inclusion, $\mathrm{id}_L$, and restriction from $X\setminus V(K_1)$ to $X\setminus V(K_2)$ form a morphism of these triangles. These maps respect composition; when the closed sets agree, the supported-section comparison is the identity under the displayed geometric identification. For $r=0$, $T_f=0$ and $E_f=A[0]$.

source.place: Tag 0A6T (lemma-local-cohomology-is-local-cohomology), statement and proof with the augmented and unaugmented alternating complexes; dualizing.tex Tag 0955 (lemma-local-cohomology-noetherian)(3) identifies right derived ideal torsion with closed support, and Tag 0956 (lemma-compute-local-cohomology-noetherian) gives the augmented localization model. Naturality in supports is the natural kernel-of-restriction construction of the localization triangle.

proof.text: Choose a complex $M$ representing $L$. The principal opens $D(f_i)$ cover $W$: a prime outside $V(K)$ omits at least one generator. Their increasing finite intersections are $D(f_{i_0}\cdots f_{i_p})$, which are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime](b), applied on $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections], sections of $\widetilde M^q$ on each such intersection are $M^q_{f_{i_0}\cdots f_{i_p}}$, with the actual localization restriction maps. For any module $N$, the sheaf kernel $\Gamma_Z(X,\widetilde N)$ is therefore $\ker(N\to\prod_iN_{f_i})$. If $f_i^{a_i}x=0$ for every $i$, enlarge each $a_i$ to be positive. Every monomial of degree $1+\sum_i(a_i-1)$ contains some $f_i^{a_i}$, so that power of $K$ kills $x$. Conversely $K^a x=0$ implies $f_i^a x=0$. Thus this kernel is exactly $\Gamma_K(N)$, naturally as a submodule of $N$. For an empty list, both kernels are all of $N$.

Each $A_g$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat]. Each term of $E_f$ and $T_f$ is a finite product of such modules (and $A$ in degree zero for $E_f$). Finite products are finite direct sums, and tensoring their sum gives the finite sum of the exact tensor functors, hence remains exact. Both complexes are bounded. Apply [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] to conclude that both are K-flat. Consequently their ordinary total tensors with any representative compute their derived tensors and preserve quasi-isomorphisms in that representative. We use Cech degree first and differential $d_{\rm Cech}+(-1)^p d_M$.

For an injective $A$-module $Q$, [lem-per-local-cohomology-cech-bound] says that $H^j(E_f\otimes_A Q)$ is $R^j\Gamma_K(Q)$ for $j\geq0$. Its complex $C^\bullet(f;Q)$ is $E_f\otimes_AQ$: for each product $g$ of generators, [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] (base ring $A$, module $A$, powers of $g$) gives $A_g\otimes_AQ\cong Q_g$, $(a/g^n)\otimes q\mapsto aq/g^n$, compatibly with the localization maps; finite products commute with $\otimes_AQ$, and the two sign conventions agree. The complex $Q[0]$ is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective]. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived], applying $\Gamma_K$ to this same complex computes its derived functor; hence its higher derived functors on $Q$ vanish. In degree zero the inclusion $\Gamma_K(Q)\hookrightarrow Q$ identifies it with the kernel of the first differential, by Step 1. There are no negative degrees. Therefore the actual augmentation $\Gamma_K(Q)[0]\to E_f\otimes_A Q$, inclusion in Cech degree zero and zero otherwise, is a quasi-isomorphism. This argument uses only the higher-degree vanishing from the cited Cech theorem; it does not assume that an unspecified isomorphism of degree-zero cohomology is the kernel inclusion.

source.place: Tag 0956 (lemma-compute-local-cohomology-noetherian), module computation, applied to injectives

proof.text: The module category is Grothendieck by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-grothendieck-abelian]. Choose a functorial resolution $M\to I$ with $I$ K-injective and all $I^q$ injective using [lem-pur-kinjective-degreewise-existence]. Apply Step 3 to each $I^q$. The double complex with rows $E_f\otimes I^q$ has Cech columns $0,\ldots,r$ and no vertical bound. Its augmentation from $\Gamma_K(I)$ is a cochain map: the horizontal differential kills ideal torsion, and the vertical differential preserves it. The finite-strip theorem [lem-sc-finite-strip-row-augmentation], with strip length $r+1$, makes the augmentation a total quasi-isomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] its source computes $R\Gamma_K(L)$. Step 2 identifies the target with $E_f\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}L$, using $E_f\otimes M\to E_f\otimes I$. All maps here are induced by the actual torsion inclusions and the functorial resolutions.

Apply [lem-sc-qcoh-complex-alternating-cech-derived-sections] to $W$ and its finite cover by $D(f_i)$; the associated modules are quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] and all intersections are affine by Step 1. Its comparison is the canonical comparison through K-injective resolutions, not merely an abstract isomorphism. The components and restriction maps of Step 1 identify the Cech total complex with $T_f\otimes M$, using termwise the isomorphisms $A_g\otimes_AM^q\cong M^q_g$ of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base], natural in $M^q$. The diagonal augmentation from $M$ sends a section to its restrictions $m/1$ on the singleton opens, so the resulting map to $R\Gamma(W,\widetilde M|_W)$ is the derived restriction. Apply the same theorem to the singleton cover $X=D(1)$: it identifies $M=\Gamma(X,\widetilde M)$ with $R\Gamma(X,\widetilde M)$ by its actual augmentation. Step 2 replaces the ordinary tensor by $T_f\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}L$.

Use [lem-per-ringed-space-supported-sections-triangle] on the Zariski ringed space $X$ and $\widetilde M$. Choose its functorial K-injective resolution $\widetilde M\to J$ with injective terms, which exists by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] on the small site of opens. The cited localization theorem gives the short exact sequence $0\to\Gamma_Z(X,J)\to\Gamma(X,J)\to\Gamma(W,J|_W)\to0$ and identifies its triangle with the derived support triangle. In particular the left term is the right derived functor of the kernel in the question. This is a theorem about Zariski module sheaves; none of the finite-coefficient etale or pro-etale support triangles is being applied to $\mathcal O_X$-modules.

Here is an explicit comparison of fibers, also fixing the maps. Write $a:M\to T_f\otimes M$. Its shifted cone is isomorphic to $E_f\otimes M$: it is the identity on $M$ and multiplies the summand corresponding to $T_f^p\otimes M^q$ by $(-1)^{p+1}$ in the shifted cone. This changes the augmented horizontal differential to the negative cone differential and leaves the required vertical sign unchanged. Put $J_W=J|_W$, K-injective by [lem-sc-derived-k-injective-restrict-open]. Let $T(J_W)$ be its Cech total complex for the same cover. There is a strictly commuting square from $a$ to $\Gamma(X,J)\to T(J_W)$, using resolution maps componentwise. The left vertical map is a quasi-isomorphism by Step 5. The right vertical map is a quasi-isomorphism by [lem-sc-qcoh-complex-alternating-cech-derived-sections] and its canonical comparison equation of [def-sc-alternating-cech-total-complex], together with [lem-sc-kinjective-alternating-cech-augmentation-quasi-iso] for $J_W$.

The augmentation $\Gamma(W,J_W)\to T(J_W)$ is a quasi-isomorphism by [lem-sc-kinjective-alternating-cech-augmentation-quasi-iso]. It gives a second strictly commuting square with identity on $\Gamma(X,J)$, from restriction to the bottom arrow of Step 7. Take the actual shifted cones of both squares, with component maps the two specified vertical maps. Each induced cone map is a quasi-isomorphism: use the degreewise split sequences $0\to B\to\operatorname{Cone}(a)\to M[1]\to0$, their natural long exact cohomology sequences [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact, lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-long-exact-naturality], and [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma], since the four surrounding component maps are isomorphisms. This gives a natural zigzag of fiber quasi-isomorphisms. The restriction arrow for $J$ is degreewise surjective by Step 6, so [lem-weil-degreewise-epi-kernel-cocone-qis] identifies its shifted cone canonically with $\Gamma_Z(X,J)$ by $(0,\mathrm{inclusion})$. Thus the augmented localization model identifies with geometric derived support, preserving both the support map and restriction. The short-exact-sequence triangle is distinguished and has natural connecting maps by [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle]. All comparisons are maps of explicit complexes, with no unspecified completion of a triangle morphism.

Apply Steps 6--8 with $M=I$ from Step 4. The termwise tilde comparison in the triangulated affine derived equivalence [new-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence-core] identifies $\widetilde I$ with $\widetilde L$, so replacing the original module representative is legitimate. The underived kernel equality of Step 1 gives the actual map $\Gamma_K(I)=\Gamma_Z(X,\widetilde I)\to\Gamma_Z(X,J)$ from a resolution $\widetilde I\to J$. In the common shifted cone of $\Gamma(X,J)\to T(J_W)$, the map from $\Gamma_K(I)$ sends $x$ to $(0,i(x))$. Indeed restrictions of a supported section to every cover intersection vanish. Both the row augmentation of Step 4 and the map through the geometric kernel have exactly this image; the cone-square zigzag therefore identifies them. Step 4 makes this map a quasi-isomorphism. Hence $R\Gamma_K(L)\cong R\Gamma_Z(X,\widetilde L)$ is the comparison induced by the actual kernel maps. Functorial resolutions make these squares natural on complex maps. All model functors invert quasi-isomorphisms by Step 2 (and the tilde equivalence), so the comparisons descend to $D(A)$ and its morphisms represented by roofs.

For $Z_1=V(K_1)\subseteq Z_2=V(K_2)$, Step 1 identifies the underived torsion functors with the respective geometric kernels on every module. These are submodules of the same module, and restriction to $X\setminus Z_2\subseteq X\setminus Z_1$ gives the kernel inclusion. On a common module resolution $I$ and a common sheaf resolution $\widetilde I\to J$, the comparison in Step 9 is induced by these literal kernel maps. Thus its square for the two supports commutes degree by degree. By [lem-per-ringed-space-supported-sections-triangle], kernel inclusion, identity, and open restriction give the claimed morphism of triangles; the comparison therefore identifies the algebraic support map with this geometric one. Kernel inclusions and restrictions compose literally. When the closed sets coincide the kernels coincide, so the comparison is the identity after the geometric identification. No comparison between arbitrary choices of Cech refinements is needed.

If $r=0$, then $K=(0)$, $Z=X$, $W=\varnothing$, $T_f=0$, $E_f=A[0]$, and $\Gamma_K$ is the identity. The triangle becomes $L\xrightarrow{1}L\to0\to L[1]$. A zero generator has empty principal open and zero localization, and is harmless. If one generator is a unit, $W=X$ and the augmentation has zero fiber. More generally the same computations allow the zero ring, repeated generators and arbitrary modules: no step required a nonempty spectrum, a proper ideal or bounded cohomology.
